paper_id: Na et al. - 2025 - QuinID Enabling FDMA-Based Fully Parallel RFID with Frequency-Selective Antenna-1
title: QuinID: Enabling FDMA-Based Fully Parallel RFID with Frequency-Selective Antenna
motivation: Large-scale logistics/production lines need to scan hundreds of RFID-tagged items simultaneously; existing parallel decoding achieves only 20% improvement
problem_framing: Traditional RFID operates in TDMA; digital FDMA cannot be implemented on tags due to ~1μW power budget; need physical-layer frequency selectivity
key_insight: Replace digital FDMA with antenna-level frequency selectivity using SAW filters—a passive, battery-free solution that bypasses tag power constraints
method_signature: SAW-based frequency-selective antenna + multi-band QuinReader with DUC/DDC and interference cancellation for FDMA operation
evaluation_criteria: Read rate (reads/sec), reading distance, tag cost, compatibility with commercial RFID systems
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: SAW introduces ~3dB insertion loss reducing range; only 5 subbands possible due to roll-off; conventional tags can interfere when present
evidence_for_taste: no existing approach achieves genuine and practical parallel RFID reading
parallel decoding algorithms only marginally accelerate the reading
a mere 20% increase in the read rate
power incurred still exceeds the affordable level
maintains compatibility with conventional RFID systems
thinking_moves: 把数字FDMA电路的功耗问题, 转化为天线滤波器的物理特性问题
不正面强攻tag芯片限制,而是从天线侧找出口
用SAW滤波器固有的高Q值特性直接满足FDMA的频选需求
